title: Which blanks make each split add up to the number?
description: Kavya's uncle stacks bricks near Mysuru. The video fills four place value splits by taking the given parts away from the whole number.
teaching_notes: One idea: add the parts given, take them from the whole, and share what is left among the blanks. Watch for a child who copies the digit of a place instead of counting all the units there.

source: Let Us Do (second set) 8 (d) to (g), more place value forms
video_script.why: The child knows place values, but has not met splits where a thousand is counted as hundreds.
video_script.substitution: Take the given parts from the whole and share what is left among the blanks.
video_script.anchor: Kavya's uncle's brick yard near Mysuru, with bricks stacked in heaps of ten thousand, thousand and hundred
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu copies the hundreds digit six. With four thousand given, the hundreds must make up the rest of the thousands too, sixteen in all.
video_script.payoff_line: take the given parts away from the whole

final_answer.value: (d) 16 Hundreds and 1 Ones; (e) 5 Thousand and 69 Ones; (f) 2 Ten Thousand and 6 Hundreds; (g) 13 Thousand and 0 Hundreds
final_answer.spoken: sixteen hundreds and one one, five thousands and sixty nine ones

video_script.design: Exercise. Hint: add the parts given and take them from the whole. Blocks stack up (ten hundreds make a thousand) in the ground part.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a brick yard with heaps of bricks of different sizes; four split statements with empty blanks, for 5,621, 7,069, 37,608 and 43,001

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.story: heaps of bricks appear in a yard
marks.ask: four numbers with empty blanks appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='story'/>Kavya's uncle has a brick yard near Mysuru, with bricks stacked in heaps of different sizes.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Your book gives four numbers split in different ways, and asks us to fill the blanks.

beats.on_screen: the items hold still and the anchor gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: 10 hundred-blocks stack into 1 thousand-block, and 10 thousand-blocks stack into 1 ten-thousand-block; a note says add the parts given and take them away from the whole

marks.fact: the blocks stack up into bigger blocks
marks.count: a thousand block breaks into ten hundred blocks

narration: <bookmark mark='fact'/>Ten hundreds make one thousand, and ten thousands make one ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Any thousand can also be counted as ten hundreds.
<bookmark mark='hint'/>Add the parts you are given, and take them away from the whole number. What is left fills the blanks. Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 5,621 = 4 Thousand + 6 Hundreds + 2 Tens + 1 One; the sum 4,000 + 600 + 20 + 1 = 4,621 appears; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.chintu: Chintu's bubble appears with the wrong blank
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>The hundreds digit is six, so the blank is six hundreds.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Four thousand, six hundreds, two tens and one one make four thousand six hundred and twenty one.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>That is one thousand short of five thousand six hundred and twenty one.

beats.on_screen: the rule line appears; 5,621 − 4,000 = 1,621 is written; the ones blank is 1; 1,621 − 21 = 1,600 and the hundreds blank shows 16 Hundreds

marks.hund: the line 1,621 − 21 = 1,600 appears and the blank shows 16 Hundreds

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Take the given parts away from the whole, and share what is left.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Take four thousand from the whole. One thousand six hundred and twenty one is left.
<bookmark mark='ones'/>The number ends in one, so the ones blank is one.
<bookmark mark='hund'/>The two tens and that one use twenty one, which leaves sixteen hundreds.

marks.e3: the blanks show 5 Thousand and 69 Ones
marks.f3: the blanks show 2 Ten Thousand and 6 Hundreds

narration: <bookmark mark='e1'/>In seven thousand and sixty nine, twenty hundreds are two thousand.
<bookmark mark='e2'/>Seven thousand and sixty nine take away two thousand leaves five thousand and sixty nine.
<bookmark mark='e3'/>No part is given for the sixty nine, so those are ones. The thousands are five.
<bookmark mark='f1'/>Seventeen thousand and eight ones come out of thirty seven thousand six hundred and eight.
<bookmark mark='f2'/>What is left is twenty thousand six hundred.
<bookmark mark='f3'/>Twenty thousand is two ten thousands, and the six hundred is six hundreds.

beats.on_screen: 43,001: 3 Ten Thousand = 30,000 and 1 One; 43,001 − 30,001 = 13,000; the blanks show 13 Thousand and 0 Hundreds

marks.g3: the blanks show 13 Thousand and 0 Hundreds

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Thirty thousand and one come out of forty three thousand and one.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Thirteen thousand is left, which is thirteen thousands.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>No hundreds are left, because thirteen thousand is a round number of thousands.

beats.on_screen: a check for the first number: 4,000 + 1,600 + 20 + 1 = 5,621

marks.check: the words add all the parts appear

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, add all the parts back together.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Four thousand, sixteen hundreds, twenty and one add up to five thousand six hundred and twenty one.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Do your parts for the other numbers add up the same way?
